medical: Resting-state functional connectivity in typically developing individuals varies across people and developmental ages.
Sensorimotor and attention network connectivity in typical development exhibits distributed individual variability.
Default-mode and frontoparietal network connectivity in typically developing individuals does not follow a single fixed individual pattern.
Measured functional connectivity can vary with head motion, acquisition quality and scanning site without indicating a specific diagnosis.
Autism-related resting-state functional connectivity differences are heterogeneous across individuals, without a universal connection-level abnormality.
In autism, atypical functional connectivity can converge at sensorimotor and attention-related brain regions and networks.
Autism-associated connectivity deviations can involve interactions between default-mode and frontoparietal control networks, with substantial individual variation.
Autism-related functional connectivity findings require cautious interpretation because age, motion and acquisition site can influence measured signals.

semantic_anchor_rule.medical: Average disease-specific prompts 1-3 and 5-7 by category; add the same mean of neutral prompts 4 and 8 to both class anchors.
semantic_anchor_rule.original: Preserve the original four texts per class from the audited SPromptGL cache.
semantic_anchor_rule.reason: The medical prompts 4 and 8 describe shared measurement caveats and are not assigned class-specific biological evidence.

prompt_claim_audit.support: Nature Mental Health 2026 normative modelling includes age-dependent interindividual variation.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Broad context; not a TD diagnostic marker.

prompt_claim_audit.support: The cited multisite study includes neurotypical controls and reports connection-level normative variability.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Sensorimotor/attention wording is descriptive context, not an ASD-vs-TD finding from this study.

prompt_claim_audit.support: Connection-level deviations are heterogeneous and no single FC estimate is extreme in more than 4% of either group.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Does not claim equal network organization across participants.

prompt_claim_audit.support: Power et al. 2012 documents motion-related changes in resting-state FC; the 2026 study spans 32 sites.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Measurement caveat only, never a TD biomarker; acquisition quality is a general caution.

prompt_claim_audit.support: The 2026 study reports individual-level connection heterogeneity and network-level convergence.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Explicitly rejects a universal connection abnormality.

prompt_claim_audit.support: The 2026 study reports convergent hypoconnectivity involving sensorimotor and attention regions/networks.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Population-level tendency with substantial individual variation.

prompt_claim_audit.support: The 2026 study reports convergent hyperconnectivity between frontoparietal and default-mode networks.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Not mapped to the CAM latent blocks or individual ROI biomarkers.

prompt_claim_audit.support: The 2026 study models age and mean framewise displacement across 32 sites; Power et al. supports the motion caveat.
prompt_claim_audit.qualification: Shared measurement context, not ASD-specific biological evidence.

texts.claims: ASD heterogeneity and network-level convergence; no universal edge abnormality; no mapping of latent CAM blocks to anatomical ROIs
